findings.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:~150 — `backupCode` is never wired into the `signIn("credentials")` call, and `formSchema` (used via `zodResolver`, which strips unknown keys) was not extended to include it; the value typed into the BackupCode field is dropped before the request, so "lost access" login can never succeed (this path also has no test, per the TODO).

[Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~200 — after `handleEnable` succeeds, `onEnable()` is only invoked from the "close" button; dismissing the dialog via Escape/overlay/`onOpenChange` at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step skips both `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, leaving the parent UI showing 2FA as disabled while it's enabled server-side, and reopening resumes on the stale step.

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:~131-155 — single-use enforcement of backup codes is a non-atomic read→decrypt→null→write with no transaction or optimistic guard; two concurrent logins with the same code both succeed, and interleaved updates can overwrite/resurrect an already-consumed code.

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — no coverage for the core new auth flows (logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code); the only backup-code test exercises display/copy/download of the codes list.

[Medium/doc_defect] apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json ("missing_backup_codes") — the message tells users to "generate them in your settings", but no settings flow can create backup codes for an account with 2FA already enabled (regeneration requires disable→re-enable, which needs the TOTP code the user just lost); users who enabled 2FA before this PR have no codes at all, so the guidance is impossible to follow.

[Low/bug] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:~148 and apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~60 — backup-code matching only strips dashes; comparison is case-sensitive with no whitespace trimming, so manually typed codes (uppercase hex, stray spaces) are rejected as "incorrect backup code" even when valid.

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~59 — `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` (and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted blob) runs on unvalidated input; a non-string `backupCode` or corrupted stored data throws an unhandled TypeError → 500 instead of a 400 error (same unguarded pattern in next-auth-options.ts).

[Low/bug] packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47 — `tabIndex={-1}` on the password-reveal toggle removes it from keyboard tab order for every `PasswordField` app-wide; keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password (accessibility regression).

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~275 — `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught; the "copied" success toast is shown even if the copy fails (permission denied) or `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (non-secure context).

[Low/performance] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~95 — the blob object URL for the download link is only revoked when a subsequent `handleSetup` replaces it; it is never revoked on unmount/dialog close, leaking the object URL and blob.

[Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:~52 — `await expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object (always truthy, no auto-retry), so the 2FA switch state is never actually verified; the added FIXME documents this but leaves the no-op assertion in place.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:~150 — `backupCode` is never wired into the `signIn("credentials")` call, and `formSchema` (used via `zodResolver`, which strips unknown keys) was not extended to include it; the value typed into the BackupCode field is dropped before the request, so "lost access" login can never succeed (this path also has no test, per the TODO).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `backupCode` field to `LoginValues` and renders `<BackupCode />` which registers `backupCode` via `react-hook-form`, and server-side auth now supports `credentials.backupCode` (next-auth authorize) plus new error handling in `login.tsx`. However, in the shown `login.tsx` changes there is no corresponding update to the form submission/sign-in payload (the existing sign-in flow is only updated to handle `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`, not to send `backupCode`). Also `useForm(... zodResolver(formSchema))` remains, and this diff does not show `formSchema` being extended to include `backupCode`, so if it’s still the old schema, zod would drop the field before submission. Together, the UI input can be collected but not actually transmitted/validated, making the “lost access” login path nonfunctional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~200 — after `handleEnable` succeeds, `onEnable()` is only invoked from the "close" button; dismissing the dialog via Escape/overlay/`onOpenChange` at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step skips both `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, leaving the parent UI showing 2FA as disabled while it's enabled server-side, and reopening resumes on the stale step.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable()` immediately. At the DisplayBackupCodes step, the Cancel button is hidden (`{step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>{t("cancel")}</Button> : null}`), and the only place that calls both `resetState()` and `onEnable()` is the explicit "close" button handler. The `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` callback is passed through without wrapping, so dismissing via Escape/overlay (which typically triggers `onOpenChange(false)`) will not invoke `resetState()` or `onEnable()`. This can leave local state stuck on DisplayBackupCodes when reopened, and the parent may not be notified to update its 2FA-enabled UI even though the server-side enable already succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — no coverage for the core new auth flows (logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code); the only backup-code test exercises display/copy/download of the codes list.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new backup-code auth logic and UI (e.g., login supports <BackupCode> with ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes handling in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx; server-side backupCode verification in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts; and disabling 2FA via backupCode in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts + DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx). However, the updated Playwright test apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts only adds assertions around the backup codes list UI (download/copy/close) and even includes a TODO to add backup code tests; it does not exercise logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with a backup code. That’s a specific, diff-grounded test gap for nontrivial new behavior rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json ("missing_backup_codes") — the message tells users to "generate them in your settings", but no settings flow can create backup codes for an account with 2FA already enabled (regeneration requires disable→re-enable, which needs the TOTP code the user just lost); users who enabled 2FA before this PR have no codes at all, so the guidance is impossible to follow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new user-facing error string `missing_backup_codes` (“No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.”) and new error paths that can emit it when `user.backupCodes` is null/absent (e.g., `next-auth-options.ts` throws `MissingBackupCodes` if `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes`, and `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` returns `MissingBackupCodes` when disabling via backup code and `!user.backupCodes`). Backup codes are only generated during `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` and shown in `EnableTwoFactorModal` after enabling, but the diff does not add any flow to generate/regenerate backup codes for accounts that already have 2FA enabled and lack `backupCodes` (legacy users). Thus, the guidance “generate them in your settings” is potentially misleading/inactionable based on the changes shown, though whether there is an existing regen flow outside this diff cannot be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~59 — `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` (and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted blob) runs on unvalidated input; a non-string `backupCode` or corrupted stored data throws an unhandled TypeError → 500 instead of a 400 error (same unguarded pattern in next-auth-options.ts).

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path executes `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` when `req.body.backupCode` is merely truthy, without validating it’s a string. If a client sends a non-string truthy value (e.g. `{}`), this will throw a `TypeError` and (absent explicit guarding/handling in the shown code) results in a 500. Similarly, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is unguarded and will throw if the decrypted blob is corrupted/non-JSON, also causing a 500. The same unguarded pattern exists in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`credentials.backupCode.replaceAll` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47 — `tabIndex={-1}` on the password-reveal toggle removes it from keyboard tab order for every `PasswordField` app-wide; keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password (accessibility regression).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the PasswordField toggle button in `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` to include `tabIndex={-1}`. This explicitly removes the password-reveal toggle from the keyboard tab sequence across the app, so keyboard-only users cannot focus/activate it via Tab, constituting an accessibility regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~275 — `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught; the "copied" success toast is shown even if the copy fails (permission denied) or `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (non-secure context).

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, the backup codes copy button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without `await`/`.then`/`.catch` and immediately shows `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`. This can (a) throw if `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (e.g., non-secure context) and (b) show a success toast even if the Promise rejects (permission denied), potentially causing an unhandled rejection and incorrect user feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:~52 — `await expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object (always truthy, no auto-retry), so the 2FA switch state is never actually verified; the added FIXME documents this but leaves the no-op assertion in place.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the test does `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, and this form asserts on the Promise object rather than the resolved boolean (and provides no locator-based auto-retry), so the switch state is effectively not verified. The newly added FIXME in the diff explicitly notes this behavior while leaving the no-op assertion in place.
